extraction.name: VoiceAssistant-Eval
extraction.description: A comprehensive benchmark for evaluating AI assistants across listening, speaking, and viewing. It contains 10,497 curated examples spanning 13 task categories and includes tasks for natural sounds, music, spoken dialogue, voice imitation, multi-turn dialogue, and multimodal vision-audio understanding.
extraction.creator: Ke Wang, Houxing Ren, Zimu Lu, Mingjie Zhan, Hongsheng Li
extraction.rai:dataCollection: VoiceAssistant-Eval is organized into three main subsets: Listening, Speaking, and Viewing. The authors collect source data from 23 audio understanding datasets, 22 datasets for spoken-interaction tasks (including text and audio datasets), and MMMU for the viewing subset. The collected text instructions are converted into audio, and role profiles/question texts are reused for role-playing tasks.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Source datasets spanning audio understanding, spoken interaction, and visual tasks, including datasets such as MMMU, VocalBench, AlpacaEval, RoleBench, AudioCaps, LibriSpeech, VCTK, CommonVoice, and others; the benchmark includes audio clips, spoken interactions, and images.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Human judges independently evaluated 10% of the model’s responses from each of the 13 tasks (1050 examples) to verify alignment with human preferences. For curation, curators reviewed items in a web-based tool and assigned a Good or Bad verdict with optional notes, using three passes: media integrity, task well-posedness, and answer validity.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Agreement between automated model-based evaluation and human judgments was analyzed using Pearson correlation coefficients and agreement rates; overall correlation was 0.92 and overall agreement rate was 96.1%.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: Independently evaluated by human judges; number of judges per item not specified.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: gpt-oss-20b was used as the automated model-based evaluation scheme.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The benchmark may carry biases from its source data and design choices; the questions and contexts are drawn from academic or synthetic sources, and the fixed set of 100 roles may encode stereotypes or omit important user personas. The monolingual focus may also limit diversity and fairness across linguistic settings.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset may be limited in diversity despite being sizable; most prompts and evaluations are in English, so it may not generalize well to more diverse linguistic settings. The benchmark also has limited model coverage, relies on automated measures and GPT-based scoring that may introduce noise and bias, lacks some task scenarios such as continuous audio-visual streaming, and is evaluated offline rather than in real-time interactive settings.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The paper highlights potential harms from misuse such as identity spoofing, harassment, fraud, privacy violations, and unequal performance across demographics, and frames the benchmark as supporting fairer and more capable multi-modal AI systems.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset involves voice/speaker-related information and role-play voice imitation, speaker similarity evaluation, and consent/provenance safeguards; it also references demographics and user personas, but does not explicitly list attributes like age or gender as collected fields.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Intended for evaluating voice assistants and benchmarking listening, speaking, and viewing capabilities; not supposed to be used for training models for cheating. The paper also recommends consent gating, watermarking/traceability for synthetic audio, and safety cards for acceptable use and abuse testing.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset and code will be publicly available under an MIT license. The authors will maintain a data governance process for auditing and removal and reserve the right to update assets if consent or licensing concerns arise.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: To increase speaker diversity, we reuse the 300 role audio clips from the role-play task as prompt audio; we also sample data from the categorized problems to balance the ratio of different tasks.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Texts were preprocessed by replacing image references with descriptive phrases, rewriting text for TTS readability and accurate pronunciation of numbers/math, and rephrasing multiple-choice options; data quality was improved through deduplication, validation, and categorization, including removing corrupted images, silent audio, ill-posed prompts, and incorrect answers.
